title: A genuine array and a string containing its text flatten to byte-identical output
rationale: The pair to vd-string-that-looks-like-array, and the reason that one cannot simply be fixed. The value domain is not injective: information is destroyed at flatten time, not at reconstruct time. This is the value-domain analogue of the key collision FlattenedPath was built to eliminate.
catchesBugClass: Non-injectivity of the value encoding - the root cause behind the whole array-inference family. It turns "the reconstructor guesses badly" into "the flattener already threw the information away".
cannotCatch: Does not cover arrays of objects, mixed-type arrays, or the _value sentinel paths. It also cannot show which of the two colliding inputs is more common in practice.

predicted.detail: Flattened output is identical to the string fixture. Both the array nesting and the element grouping are wrong; the correct answer is an object holding an array, not an array of three objects.

configDescription: defaults; paired flat-map equality against vd-string-that-looks-like-array
